text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Canada offers to lead aid force: South Africa also willing to committ troops for humanitarian relief mission in Zaire.
- Relief convoy stalled in Zaire: Talks under way over distribution.
- Moscow slaying terrifies foreigners: Investors fear they could be next.
- Hunger crisis faces summit: Wide starvation exists at time of record food production.
- U.S. called shots in Somalia: Canadian colonel resented 'scandalous' degree of control.
- Taxes for education may shift to province: Panel to propose major swap of powers.
- Funds miss boat on banks: Managers didn't own enough of hot sector to cash in on surge of prices.
- Sherritt International to sink $300 million into Cuba.
- No plan B on pay cut, Canadian Air chief says: Carrier preparing to shut down if employees spurn proposal.
- Sherritt to expand in Cuba: Analysts surprised by size of deal as company snubs U.S. Helms-Burton law with $600 million in debentures to finance projects in country.
- Phone, cable companies can buy into latest competition.
